title: Particles of Matter
subject: Chemistry
objective: Matter looks continuous, but it is made of extremely small particles. Two crystals of potassium permanganate can colour glass after glass of water.

fill.q: Matter is made of very tiny ____.
Matter is not ____; it is made of particles.
In the KMnO₄ activity the colour stays even after many ____.
Particles of matter are too small to see even with an ordinary ____.

tf.q: A few crystals of KMnO₄ contain a huge number of particles.
tf.explain: The colour spreads through many dilutions.

tf.q: Matter is one continuous block with no particles.
Particles of matter can be seen with a hand lens.
Dissolving sugar spreads its particles through the water.
tf.explain: The sugar is still there, as particles.

ar.a: The colour of KMnO₄ solution remains after many dilutions.
ar.r: One crystal contains millions of tiny particles.
ar.explain: Enough particles remain after each dilution; R explains A.

ar.a: We can see particles of matter with a school microscope.
ar.r: Particles of matter are extremely small.
ar.explain: A is false; R is true.

mcq.q: The KMnO₄ dilution activity shows that particles are:
Particles of matter are best described as:

short.q: Describe the KMnO₄ dilution activity and its conclusion.
short.solution: Dissolve a few crystals in water and keep diluting. The colour stays through many dilutions, so a few crystals hold millions of tiny particles: matter is made of very small particles.

short.q: Why does sugar seem to disappear in water?
short.solution: Its particles spread into the spaces between water particles; it is still present, which we can taste.

match.explain: Everyday activities reveal the particle nature of matter.
